items.target: Identify Micah’s mother as the person who cursed the stolen silver.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: Micah tells his mother that he heard her curse the silver taken from her: “我听见你咒诅它”.

answer_support.evidence: The speaker addresses his mother as “你”; she is therefore the person who cursed the silver.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: Only Micah’s mother is identified as having cursed the silver.

context_sufficiency.evidence: Verses 17:1–2 identify Micah, his mother, and the silver involved.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question identifies the silver but does not name the person who cursed it.

items.target: Identify all three peoples whom God helped Uzziah fight.

target_preservation.evidence: The final question preserves the original question and its three-part answer: Philistines, Arabs in Gur Baal, and Meunites.

question_support.evidence: Verse 26:7 explicitly states that God helped him fight these peoples; 26:6 identifies him as Uzziah.

answer_support.evidence: The expected answer reproduces the complete list in 26:7.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: The passage supplies one complete three-part list of opponents in this help relation.

context_sufficiency.evidence: The surrounding verses establish Uzziah as the referent of “他” in 26:7.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question names God and Uzziah but does not disclose the opponents.

mcq_validity.evidence: D matches 26:7 exactly. A substitutes the tribute-paying Ammonites; B changes the Arabs’ location and includes Ammonites; C supplies an unsupported list. E is false because the list is explicit.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: Opponents against whom God provided military help

items.target: Identify the man of God as the person who prayed for the king.

target_preservation.evidence: The final question is unchanged and still asks who actually prayed for the king, matching the original answer “the man of God”.

question_support.evidence: Verse 13:6 states both the king’s request and its fulfillment: “神人就为王祷告”.

answer_support.evidence: The passage supports “神人” but never says he came from Judah. The expected answer adds an unsupported geographical identification.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: The man of God is the only person said to pray for the king.

context_sufficiency.evidence: The supplied verse uniquely identifies the prayer event and its agent, although it does not establish that agent’s origin.

answer_leakage.evidence: Saying that the king asked the man of God to pray does not itself establish who fulfilled the request.

mcq_validity.evidence: Key A adds “从犹大来的”, which the passage does not establish. B and C are not identified as praying, and D is not identified in the passage. E cannot repair the missing support for A: the text identifies a man of God, but not the qualified identity required by A.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: Agent who fulfilled a request for prayer

items.target: Identify Paul’s planned departure the next day as the reason he continued speaking until midnight.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: Verse 20:7 explicitly connects Paul’s planned departure with his speaking: “由于保罗第二天准备离开”.

answer_support.evidence: The expected answer gives the stated reason: he intended to leave the following day.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: Only the next-day departure is given as the reason for his extended speaking.

context_sufficiency.evidence: Verse 20:7 contains Paul, the midnight endpoint, and the reason for speaking.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question supplies the action and endpoint, not the reason.

items.target: Identify Sceva’s seven sons as those who fled the house injured after being overpowered.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: Verse 19:16 states that the possessed man overpowered them and that they fled the house injured.

answer_support.evidence: Verse 19:14 identifies the participants as Sceva’s seven sons; 19:16 describes what happened to “他们”.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: The fleeing group is the same group identified as Sceva’s seven sons; “the exorcists” would be an equivalent contextual description.

context_sufficiency.evidence: Verses 19:13–16 supply the group’s identity and the pronoun chain leading to their flight.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question describes the attack and escape but does not name those who escaped.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: Identity of people suffering an attack and fleeing

items.target: Identify the prophet’s own city as the first destination to which he brought the man of God’s body.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: The passage identifies “那带他回来的先知” and says he brought the body back to his own city before its burial in his tomb.

answer_support.evidence: Verse 13:29 explicitly says “带回自己的城里”.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: His own city is the first stated destination. The donkey is the means of transport, and the tomb is the subsequent burial location.

context_sufficiency.evidence: Verses 13:26–30 identify the prophet, the body, its transport, and the later burial.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question identifies the prophet by his earlier action but does not reveal the body’s destination.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: First destination in a transport-and-burial sequence

items.target: Identify tomorrow as the proposed day for eating the other woman’s son.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: “她们约定” presupposes a mutual agreement. The displayed passage reports one woman’s proposal, “明天我们就吃我的儿子”, but does not state the other woman’s acceptance.

answer_support.evidence: “Tomorrow” is the explicit proposed day for eating the speaking woman’s own son, who is the other woman relative to the complainant.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: Only one day is specified for eating that woman’s son: “明天”.

context_sufficiency.evidence: The reporting frame and quotation distinguish the complainant from “那妇人” and identify whose son is proposed for tomorrow.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question asks for the day without supplying it.

items.target: Identify the 2,600 family leaders as those commanding the 307,500 trained soldiers.

target_preservation.evidence: The final question preserves the original troop number, command relation, and answer identifying the 2,600 family leaders.

question_support.evidence: Verse 26:13 describes 307,500 trained soldiers as “他们统领的军队”, referring back to the leaders in 26:12.

answer_support.evidence: The antecedent of “他们” is the 2,600 family leaders named immediately before it.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: The specified troop total is explicitly linked to those leaders, not to the officials responsible for registration.

context_sufficiency.evidence: Verses 26:12–13 provide both the commanders and the troop count, allowing the pronoun to be resolved.

answer_leakage.evidence: The troop count anchors the question but does not disclose the commanders.

mcq_validity.evidence: D matches the explicit command relation. A supervises the registration described in 26:11; B records the army; C is its king and owner but is not the stated referent of “他们统领”. E is contradicted by 26:12–13.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: Commanders of a specified military force

items.target: Identify the man of God as the person whom the king ordered seized.

target_preservation.evidence: The final question is unchanged and still tests the identity given by the original answer, “the man of God”.

question_support.evidence: After hearing the man of God speak, the king says “捉住他”, supporting the question’s seizure order.

answer_support.evidence: The passage identifies the target as the man of God but does not say that he came from Judah, as the expected answer asserts.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: In 13:4, “他” in the seizure command refers to the man of God whose words the king has just heard.

context_sufficiency.evidence: The displayed sentence supplies the king, the triggering speech, and the person targeted by the command; it does not supply that person’s origin.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question asks for the command’s target without identifying him.

mcq_validity.evidence: Key A includes the unsupported origin “从犹大来的”. B is the king issuing the command; C and D are not identified as its target. E does not fix the unsupported key: the target is identifiable as a man of God, but his asserted origin is not established.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: Target of an order to seize someone

items.target: Identify the five scouts’ taking the idols from Micah’s house as the first event involving the idols in the displayed sequence.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: The first displayed event involving the idols is the five scouts entering and taking them in 18:17–18.

answer_support.evidence: Verse 18:17 identifies the five men and their taking the objects; 18:18 identifies the house as Micah’s.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: The initial taking precedes the priest’s later taking of objects in 18:20. Verses 18:17–18 repeat and elaborate the initial action rather than supply incompatible first events.

context_sufficiency.evidence: The displayed sequence identifies the idols, the initial takers, the house, and the subsequent departure.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question mentions the idols but does not disclose what first happened to them.

items.target: Identify the two companies off Sabbath duty as those instructed to guard the LORD’s temple for the king.

target_preservation.evidence: The final question retains the original guarding assignment, location, beneficiary, and answer identifying the two off-duty companies.

question_support.evidence: Verse 11:7 explicitly orders a group to “为王看守耶和华的殿”.

answer_support.evidence: The group receiving that specific assignment is “那两班安息日不值勤的”.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: The exact assignment of guarding the LORD’s temple for the king is attached to the two off-duty companies in 11:7.

context_sufficiency.evidence: The passage supplies the instructions and distinguishes the companies by duty status and assigned positions.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question gives the assignment but not the group receiving it.

mcq_validity.evidence: A matches 11:7. B is assigned the palace, C names a different station, and D names officers addressed in the broader instructions rather than the companies specified for this task. E is false because 11:7 gives the answer.

meaning_profile.semantic_relation: Group assigned a particular guarding duty

items.target: Identify speaking until daybreak as Paul’s last stated action before leaving.

target_preservation.evidence: No original question, original answer, or explicit intended target is supplied.

question_support.evidence: Verse 20:11 gives an ordered sequence ending with “讲到天亮才离开”, supporting a question about the last action before departure.

answer_support.evidence: The expected answer matches the action immediately preceding departure: continuing to speak until daylight.

answer_uniqueness.evidence: Going upstairs, breaking bread, and eating occur before the final speaking; no later action by Paul before departure is stated.

context_sufficiency.evidence: Verse 20:11 explicitly identifies Paul and connects his final speaking with his departure.

answer_leakage.evidence: The question supplies the departure endpoint without naming the preceding action.
